name: Astaxanthin
short: Case report: a 69-year-old on warfarin and aspirin had bruising a day after adding astaxanthin, larger next day; INR rose to 10.38. Review, 87 human studies of natural astaxanthin: no safety concerns.
text: A safety review of 87 human studies of natural astaxanthin supplementation found that none reported safety concerns, 35 of them at intakes of 12 mg/day or more; the review notes that a European regulatory acceptable daily intake of 2 mg was based on a rat study of synthetic astaxanthin, which it describes as chemically different from natural astaxanthin. A systematic review of eleven clinical studies on skin health reported no serious adverse events, but most studies were small and conducted in healthy Japanese women. One case report described a 69-year-old woman taking warfarin, aspirin and other medicines who developed bruising one day after starting astaxanthin, which had spread by the next day, and whose INR rose from 1.4 to 10.38; after warfarin and astaxanthin were withheld and vitamin K was given, her INR was 1.43 two days later and the bruising had improved, and the authors judged the relationship between the bleeding and astaxanthin probable. This is a single case report, and the abstract does not say how much astaxanthin was taken.
